subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does the gateway security model confirm that observing or predicting an event `seq` value cannot authorize a request, resume another socket, or bypass connection and device authentication?
rationale: Source and protocol documentation contradict the reported primitive, but the protected security classification requires a human owner to confirm the intended trust boundary before closure.

options.title: Confirm and close
options.body: Confirm that `seq` is non-secret ordering metadata and close the report as unsupported by the current gateway protocol.

options.title: Request an exploit trace
options.body: Keep the report open temporarily and ask for a current-main frame transcript showing an unauthorized request accepted after using a predicted sequence value.

recommendation.title: Confirm and close
recommendation.body: Confirm that `seq` is non-secret ordering metadata and close the report as unsupported by the current gateway protocol.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work directly hardened authentication and origin validation in the affected WebSocket connection path.
